title: Run axe in every A11Y spec and assert on its violations

facts.note: Encodes an `a11y` token in the file basename: `a11y` preceded by the start of the basename or one of `.`, `-`, `_`, and followed by one of `.`, `-`, `_` (every combination of left and right boundary is listed, e.g. `a11y-check.e2e.ts`, `checkout_a11y_check.e2e.ts`, `checkout.a11y.e2e.ts`). Equivalent basename regex: `(^|[._-])a11y([._-]|$)`. Match the basename only, not directory names, and not `a11y` embedded in a longer word. Never match files under node_modules, dist, build or _generated.

Alternative identification: the spec carries an `A11Y` test URN. Needs a parser for test URNs in the file. Either this or the filename token is required; neither task words nor an `.e2e.ts` suffix is enough on its own.

browser_spec = a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright, or any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), so a misnamed one is still judged. A unit test that only mentions a journey URN inside a string is not a browser spec. Needs a header-comment parser and Playwright-config awareness. Used together with the A11Y identification above, not as a substitute for it.
Detector finding: AxeBuilder import or `.analyze()` call missing, or no violations assertion that can fail.
Writing or editing an accessibility spec.

fires: A new `*.a11y.e2e.ts` spec navigates to a page and asserts only on visible text, without running axe
A spec named `a11y-check.e2e.ts` or `checkout_a11y_check.e2e.ts` imports AxeBuilder but never calls `.analyze()`
A spec with an `A11Y` test URN calls `new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze()` but never asserts on `violations`
A misnamed test file whose header has a `// URN: test:journey:…` marker and an A11Y test URN does not run axe
doesNotFire: A browser spec that has no `A11Y` test URN and no `a11y` token in its file name, even if the task mentions accessibility
A `*.e2e.ts` file under a directory named `a11y` that has no `a11y` token in its own file name and no A11Y URN
A file whose basename contains `a11y` only inside a longer word (no `.`, `-`, `_` or start-of-name boundary around it) and has no A11Y URN
A unit test that only mentions a journey or A11Y URN inside a string literal

given: A spec is identified as accessibility: it has an `A11Y` test URN, or its file name contains an `a11y` token
when: The tester writes or changes that spec
then: The spec must run the axe harness and assert on the returned `violations` in a way that can fail. This requires importing `AxeBuilder` from `@axe-core/playwright` (under any local name) and calling `new AxeBuilder(...).analyze()`.
prefer: Assert that there are no violations: `toEqual([])`, `toHaveLength(0)`, or `toBe(0)` on the count
Or use a bounded assertion: `toBeLessThanOrEqual(n)` or `toBeLessThan(n)`
`const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze(); expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);`
avoid: An accessibility spec that navigates the page but never runs axe
Running axe and then never asserting on the result
Tautological assertions that cannot fail, such as `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)`. These do not count as assertions
why: An accessibility spec that navigates but never runs axe, or never asserts on the result, passes no matter what state the page is actually in.
evidence: The spec file imports `AxeBuilder` from `@axe-core/playwright` (any local binding name)
The spec calls `new AxeBuilder(...).analyze()`, and the result's `violations` is passed to one of `toEqual([])`, `toHaveLength(0)`, `toBe(0)`, `toBeLessThanOrEqual(n)` or `toBeLessThan(n)`
verifier_detail: Identify accessibility specs only by an `A11Y` test URN or an `a11y` token in the file name. Token = `a11y` in the basename bounded on the left by start-of-name or `.`/`-`/`_` and on the right by `.`/`-`/`_` or end-of-name (regex on basename: `(^|[._-])a11y([._-]|$)`). Directory names, substrings inside other words, and task wording do not count.

browser_spec: a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright, or any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`). A misnamed one is therefore still judged. A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not a browser spec.
Resolve the AxeBuilder import under any local alias.

Accepted matchers on `violations` are equal-to-none (`toEqual([])`, `toHaveLength(0)`, `toBe(0)`) and bounded (`toBeLessThanOrEqual(n)`, `toBeLessThan(n)`). Reject tautologies such as `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)`. They are not assertions.
Never scan vendored and generated trees (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`).
Severity 3. Disposition: strict (as stated in the source; the source does not further define its enforcement semantics).
audit: Original name/summary: An A11Y spec runs axe and asserts on its violations.

additions.justification: Derived from the statement, the browser_spec term and the exceptions so that activation can be tested. They add no new obligation or identification signal.

additions.text: Basename glob patterns and equivalent regex `(^|[._-])a11y([._-]|$)` for the `a11y` filename token
additions.justification: Observable encoding of the source's 'an `a11y` token in its file name'. The token boundary set (start, `.`, `-`, `_`) is an interpretation of 'token'; it covers leading (`a11y-check`), dotted, dashed and underscore-delimited interior tokens, and is limited to the basename so it matches nothing broader than the source.

trace.note: Mirror relationship and bare 'strict' label kept verbatim; no enforcement semantics added
